title: How to launch a new medical device to cardiologists
overview: How to launch a new medical device: a medical device launch strategy for reaching interventional cardiologists, from go-to-market planning to a stent launch campaign.
author: Made Clear
body:
Knowing how to launch a new medical device is about more than a press release and a congress booth. Interventional cardiologists are sceptical, busy and loyal to the tools they know. A successful medtech product launch gives them a clear reason to change, evidence they trust and the confidence to use the device on their next patient.

This guide sets out the medical device launch strategy we've seen work, drawing on launches and adoption campaigns we've delivered across cardiology.

1. Understand the barrier to adoption

Every launch has to overcome a specific doubt. Find it before you write a word. For iVascular's Angiolite stent, the barrier was disbelief: physicians didn't believe one stent could work as well in large vessels as in small ones. Our Big Discrepancies, Big Solutions film tackled that head on, filming the stent expanding inside life-sized transparent artery models so cardiologists could see it for themselves. A stent launch campaign that addresses the real doubt is worth more than one that lists every feature.

2. Map everyone involved in the decision

A medical device go to market strategy has to reach more than the physician. Hospital administrators, procurement, nurses and technologists all influence adoption, and they care about different things.

For Philips ICE in the Heart, we built a three-part campaign around the adoption journey of the VeriSight Pro ICE catheter: a top-line interview recommending the device to the medical team, a how-to animation for physicians, and a value explainer showing hospital administrators how it saves time and money.

3. How to market a medical device to cardiologists

Cardiologists respond to evidence, technique and the experience of their peers. The content that moves them:

  • Is led by KOLs they respect, discussing real cases.
  • Shows the device in use, in the cath lab or in a clear procedural animation.
  • Explains the mechanism, especially when it's new or counterintuitive.
  • Respects their intelligence, with balanced claims and honest data.

4. Educate before and at launch

The fastest launches start education early. For Shockwave Medical, we produced The Calcium Masterclass, a 10-part peer-to-peer programme for US interventional cardiologists on the eve of intravascular lithotripsy's FDA approval. Over 5,500 cardiologists took part, spending an average of 28 minutes each. The programme helped Shockwave dramatically reduce the time from product launch to adoption across all approved markets, delivering 271% revenue growth.

5. How to reach interventional cardiologists

Interventional cardiologists are concentrated in a few places, and a launch plan should use all of them:

  • Congresses: EuroPCR, TCT, ACC, ESC and SCAI gather the field in one place. Booth content, symposia and KOL interviews filmed on site extend the launch far beyond the hall. See how to make the most of your KOLs at congresses.
  • Education platforms: peer-to-peer programmes and live broadcasts reach physicians who can't travel.
  • The field team: sales reps need content they can show in a hospital in a few minutes.
  • Professional networks and social: short clips and teasers drive physicians to the longer content. For The Radiation Problem, short teaser films promoted a live launch on a network of 68,000 cardiologists.

6. Make the launch memorable

At a busy congress, every company is launching something. Formats that let physicians experience the device stand out. The Curious Case of Coronary Calcium, a 25-minute VR experience presented by two leading interventional cardiologists, has been deployed at major international congresses and used as a field sales tool by Shockwave's commercial teams.

7. Equip the field team

Launches succeed or stall in hospitals, one conversation at a time. Give reps short, clear content they can use with physicians and administrators: procedural animations, KOL clips, value explainers and immersive demos. Train them to use it well.

8. Keep going after launch day

Adoption takes months, not days. Plan a sustained programme: new cases, new voices, new data and local versions for each market. Measure what physicians do, not just what they watch.

A launch checklist

  • What single doubt must the launch overcome?
  • Who influences the decision, and what does each of them need?
  • Which KOLs will carry the message?
  • What will physicians see at the launch congress, and what will they take away?
  • What will the field team use in hospitals the week after?
  • How will you keep the conversation going for the next year?
